name: LM75BIMX-5_NOPB
title: LM75B, LM75C: 9-bit I2C digital temperature sensor with over-temperature output
summary: The LM75B and LM75C measure their own die temperature with a bandgap sensor and a sigma-delta converter and report it as a 9-bit two's-complement word (0.5 °C per step) over a two-wire I2C-compatible bus running to 400 kHz. Three address pins give eight bus addresses. An open-drain O.S. output trips at a programmable limit with programmable hysteresis, polarity, comparator or interrupt behaviour and a fault count of 1, 2, 4 or 6, and with its power-up defaults (80 °C on, 75 °C off, active low) the part works as a thermostat with no bus at all. Each part is trimmed at 3.3 V (-3 suffix) or 5 V (-5 suffix); LM75BIMX-5/NOPB is the LM75B, 5 V grade, in SOIC-8 on a 2500-piece reel.
key_figures: 0.25 mA typ; 0.5 mA max (LM75B), 1 mA max (LM75C) over temperature
4 µA typ at 3 V, 6 µA typ at 5 V
I2C-compatible, up to 400 kHz, address 1001 A2 A1 A0
TOS 80 °C, THYST 75 °C, comparator mode, active low

notes: The -3 parts are tested and specified for accuracy at +VS = 3.3 V and the -5 parts at +VS = 5 V; all run from 3 V to 5.5 V.
IM is SOIC (D) and IMM is VSSOP (DGK); an X after IM or IMM is the large reel.

The characteristics tables also name the LM75C grades LM75CIM-3, LM75CIM-5, LM75CIMM-3 and LM75CIMM-5. The LM75C has no input filter on SDA and SCL and no bus timeout, and differs in quiescent current, ESD and output leakage.
VSSOP marking: T01B for the 3.3 V LM75B, T00B for the 5 V LM75B.

pins.name: SDA
pins.function: Bidirectional serial data of the I2C bus. Needs a pull-up resistor or current source from the controller side.

pins.name: SCL
pins.function: Serial clock input of the I2C bus; the part never drives it. Needs a pull-up resistor or current source.

pins.name: O.S.
pins.function: Over-temperature output with no internal pull-up. Normally pulled up and taken to a controller interrupt input.

pins.name: GND
pins.function: Supply ground. In VSSOP this pin is tied directly to the die and is its main thermal path.

pins.name: A2

pins.name: A1

pins.name: A0

pins.name: +VS
pins.function: Supply, 3 V to 5.5 V DC. Decouple with 100 nF at the pin and 10 µF of bulk capacitance close by.

circuits.title: Typical application
circuits.description: The sensor on a host's I2C bus. A 100 nF capacitor decouples +VS unless the part sits close to the processor. A0 to A2 are strapped high or low to pick one of eight addresses, SDA and SCL run to the host, and O.S., left at its active-low default, joins the processor's interrupt line, which several open-drain O.S. outputs may share as a wired OR.

parts.note: typical; may be omitted when the part sits next to the processor

notes: O.S. is set to active low so that several parts can share one interrupt line.

circuits.title: Simple fan controller, interface optional
circuits.description: A 12 V, 300 mA fan switched by the sensor's O.S. output. R1 pulls O.S. up and drives the base of Q1; Q1's collector, pulled up by R2, drives the gate of the N-channel MOSFET Q2 that sinks the fan current. With O.S. at its active-low default, an over-temperature pulls Q1's base low, Q1 turns off, R2 lifts Q2's gate and the fan runs. R3 ties the address pins, SDA and SCL high for stand-alone use.

parts.note: optional pull-up for stand-alone use, recommended

notes: When the bus is used, O.S. is programmed active high and wired straight to Q2's gate.

circuits.title: Simple thermostat, interface optional
circuits.description: A heater thermostat on 5 V. O.S., pulled up by R1, drives the base of the NPN Q1, which switches the coil of the 5 V relay K1; D1 clamps the coil's turn-off spike. The relay contact closes the heater's loop to its own supply. With the power-up defaults, O.S. goes low above 80 °C and releases at 75 °C, so Q1 holds the relay pulled in while the part is cool and drops it out when hot. R2 ties the address pins, SDA and SCL high for stand-alone use.

parts.note: optional pull-up for stand-alone use, recommended
pins: COIL1, COIL2 coil; COM, NO contact

circuits.title: Temperature sensor with loudmouth alarm (barking watchdog)
circuits.description: An audible over-temperature alarm. O.S., pulled up by R1, drives the SHUTDOWN input of an LM4861 audio power amplifier that drives a speaker bridged between its two outputs. The amplifier's inverting input takes feedback from Vo1 through R5 and through a three-section RC ladder (C3 to C5 with R2, R6, R4 to ground) coupled in by C2, a phase-shift network that makes it sound a tone whenever O.S. lets it run. BYPASS is decoupled by C1 and also biases +IN. R3 ties the address pins, SDA and SCL high for stand-alone use.

parts.note: optional pull-up for stand-alone use, recommended

notes: Misprint: the 10 kΩ from the middle RC node to ground is also labelled R3, the same as the stand-alone pull-up; it should read R6.

operation.text: A silicon bandgap sensor feeds a sigma-delta converter (1-bit D/A loop and 10-bit decimation filter) that yields 9-bit readings. The latest result is always readable; a bus access interrupts the conversion in progress and it restarts once the access ends.

The LM75B has everything the LM75C has plus a low-pass filter on SDA and SCL for noisy buses, and a bus timeout: SDA held low longer than tTIMEOUT returns the LM75B to idle with SDA released, ready for a new start. The timeout does not run in shutdown.

O.S. acts as a thermostat: it goes active when the temperature rises past TOS and returns inactive when it falls below THYST. Uses named for it: switching a fan, starting a system shutdown, cutting the clock rate. Shutdown does not clear O.S. in this mode; its state during shutdown is undefined.

Crossing above TOS sets O.S., and it stays set until any register is read or the part is put into shutdown. After that reset the next event is the temperature falling below THYST, which sets O.S. again until the next read. Trigger events are the same in both modes; only the latching differs.

Below about 1.7 V of supply the part counts as off; rising through that level loads the defaults: TOS = 80 °C and THYST = 75 °C, the comparator behaviour, an active-low O.S., and the pointer at 00 (temperature). With no bus connected the part runs as a thermostat on these values. Tying A2, A1, A0, SCL and SDA together to +VS through 10 kΩ (or each pin through its own 10 kΩ) is optional but recommended for noise immunity.

The part is an I2C slave: SCL is input only and SDA is bidirectional. A write sends the address byte, then the pointer byte, then one data byte for the configuration register or two for TOS and THYST. A read of the register the pointer already selects is the address byte followed by the data bytes; to change the pointer first, send address, pointer, a repeated start, then the address again. Data come most significant byte first, MSB first, so a host can stop after the first byte; the part accepts either ACK or NACK on the last byte.

operation.topic: Bus lock-up from a short read
operation.text: Reading only 8 bits of a 16-bit register when D7 is 0 can leave the part holding SDA low, blocking the bus until at least 9 more clocks are sent. The master may instead clock until SDA goes high and then issue a stop, which resets the part.

Setting the shutdown bit cuts the supply current to a few microamps. The bus stays alive, so TOS, THYST and configuration can still be read and written; bus traffic adds a little current. In interrupt mode shutdown clears O.S.; on the LM75B the timeout is off.
To avoid false trips in noisy surroundings, O.S. is set only after 1, 2, 4 or 6 out-of-limit conversions in a row, chosen by configuration bits D4 and D3.

O.S. is open-drain at both polarities and has no internal pull-up. Choose the pull-up as high in value as the system allows, to keep sink current and the self-heating it causes low; 30 kΩ is the most that still gives a 2 V high against the IOH leakage. Polarity is set by configuration bit D2, active low by default.

Put 100 nF and 10 µF close to +VS so that noise from a noisy or high-impedance supply does not reach the measurement. Operation is specified from 2.7 V to 5.5 V in the supply recommendations and from 3 V to 5.5 V in the recommended operating conditions. SCL and SDA each need a 10 kΩ pull-up when the bus is used.

The part reads its own die temperature, and the leads are the best path from die to board, so it tracks the temperature of the board it sits on; the plastic body couples more weakly to the air. In VSSOP the GND pin connects straight to the die and dominates; in SOIC no pin does and all leads count about equally. For a probe the part can sit in a sealed metal tube lowered into a liquid bath or threaded into a tank. Part and wiring must stay dry and insulated, above all where cold brings condensation; conformal coatings such as Humiseal or epoxy paint or dip are used for this.

Keep the bus away from switching supplies and let fast digital lines cross SDA and SCL at right angles. The LM75C has no input filter: noise above about 400 mVpp (its typical input hysteresis), overshoot past +VS by more than 300 mV or undershoot below GND by more than 300 mV can stop it communicating, seen mostly as missing acknowledges. Long traces and many parts on the bus call for proper termination; series resistance in SDA and SCL damps noise and ringing, and for the LM75C a 5 kΩ resistor in series with SCL right at the pin is the usual remedy.

In the typical layout C1 sits at pin 8 with its ground end on a short path to GND, the SDA and SCL pull-ups R1 and R2 sit beside pins 1 and 2 and share one supply trace back to +VS, pin 4 runs straight to ground, and O.S. and A0 to A2 leave as plain traces.
